_meta.sources: VA CBT-I Therapist Manual (public domain); AASM CBT-I clinical practice guidelines; SleepioRx framework; standard CBT-I literature (Perlis, Edinger, Morin)

meta.name: Digital CBT-I Protocol
meta.based_on: Evidence-based framework grounded in AASM CBT-I guidelines and the VA CBT-I therapist manual.
meta.evidence: Multiple RCTs of digital CBT-I; npj Digital Medicine (2025) and related dCBT-I trials.

components_rating.sleep_restriction: 1A (Sleep Restriction + Stimulus Control, Level I recommendation in CBT-I guidelines)
components_rating.sleep_hygiene: 2A (Sleep Hygiene Education, Level II — adjunctive, not standalone)

sleep_restriction_therapy.description: Restrict time in bed to increase sleep drive (Homeostatic Sleep Pressure).
sleep_restriction_therapy.mechanism: Reduces wakefulness in bed → increases sleep efficiency → improves sleep quality → time in bed gradually expands.

implementation.TIB_calculation: Time in Bed = Out-of-bed time − Into-bed time.
implementation.TST_calculation: Total Sleep Time = TIB − Sleep Onset Latency (SOL) − Wake After Sleep Onset (WASO).
implementation.prescription: Initial TIB = mean TST over last 1–2 weeks (but no less than 5 hours).
implementation.adjustment: Weekly review: if SE > 85%, expand TIB by 15–30 min; if SE < 80%, reduce TIB.

sleep_restriction_therapy.AI_adaptation: In a pre-sleep companion context, don't enforce strict window calculations. Instead, gently guide: 'Try going to bed 15–30 minutes later than usual tonight, and see if you fall asleep faster.' (Light-touch sleep restriction.)

stimulus_control.description: Rebuild the conditioned association between bed and sleep; weaken the bed-wakefulness link.

core_instructions.instruction: Only get into bed when you're clearly sleepy.
core_instructions.rationale: Reduces wakeful time in bed; strengthens 'bed = sleep' association.

core_instructions.instruction: If you can't fall asleep within ~20 minutes, get up and go to another room until sleepy again.
core_instructions.rationale: Breaks the 'awake = in bed' conditioned response.

core_instructions.instruction: Use the bed only for sleep and intimacy — no phones, TV, work, or worrying in bed.
core_instructions.rationale: Weakens the bed's association with non-sleep activities.

core_instructions.instruction: Get up at the same time every day (including weekends) to anchor the circadian rhythm.
core_instructions.rationale: Stabilizes the body clock and builds sleep drive.

core_instructions.instruction: Avoid daytime naps. If you must, keep them under 20 minutes and before 3 PM.

stimulus_control.AI_adaptation: In a pre-sleep companion context, guide a brief 'sleep onset ritual': 'When you get into bed tonight, just do one thing — close your eyes and let your breath happen. No counting, no trying. Just waiting.' (Light-touch stimulus control.)

cognitive_restructuring.description: Identify and reframe catastrophic cognitions about sleep.
target_cognitive_distortions: All-or-Nothing: 'I must get 8 hours or tomorrow is wrecked.'
Catastrophizing: 'If I don't sleep, I'll have a breakdown / die / lose my job.'
Pre-sleep monitoring: 'How long have I been awake? How long until the alarm?'
Fortune-telling: 'I know I won't sleep tonight either.'
Emotional reasoning: 'Because I can't sleep, something must be very wrong with me.'
Socratic_questioning_sequence: How true is this thought? Is 'I'll die if I don't sleep' backed by data?
Even if the worst happened, would it really be as bad as it feels?
Any counter-evidence? Have there been nights when you slept little and still got through the day?
If you didn't believe this thought, how would you look at tonight?
Right now, what does your body actually need — sleep, or just calm?
cognitive_restructuring.AI_adaptation: Don't attempt deep cognitive restructuring (that's the therapist's job). Instead: 1) gently surface a catastrophic thought; 2) offer a counter-example; 3) shift attention to bodily sensation.

sleep_hygiene.description: Optimize sleep environment and behavior (Level II recommendation; adjunctive, not standalone).

environmental.rationale: Core body temperature drop is a sleep-onset trigger.

environmental.recommendation: Total darkness (blackout curtains or eye mask)
White noise or earplugs (steady background better than sudden noise)
Comfortable mattress and pillow — not too firm, not too soft

behavioral.effect: Blocks adenosine receptors; delays sleep pressure.
Speeds onset but fragments REM and causes early waking.
Blue light suppresses melatonin; delays sleep onset.
Raises temperature and activates cortisol; delays sleep.

behavioral.do: Get 10–15 minutes of bright natural light right after waking
Moderate aerobic exercise (finishing 3+ hours before bed)

sleep_hygiene.AI_adaptation: Don't deliver checklists. Weave hygiene into conversation: 'Did you have coffee this afternoon?' — light, conversational, never preachy.

paradoxical_intention.description: Core technique for 'sleep-effort syndrome' insomnia (Level A recommendation).
paradoxical_intention.mechanism: Deliberately trying to stay awake removes the anxiety about sleep, breaking the 'try harder → more awake' cycle.
paradoxical_intention.indication: Sleep-onset insomnia + strong pre-sleep anxiety + over-monitoring of sleep state in bed.

AI_instruction_sequence.script: I've noticed you're monitoring whether you're close to sleep. Here's the thing — that effort itself is what keeps you awake.

So tonight, I want to invite an experiment: don't try to fall asleep. I mean it. You don't have to do anything to make sleep happen. Just keep your eyes lightly open, or gently closed, and tell yourself: 'I'm not going to force sleep tonight. I'm just resting here.'
When you really put down 'must sleep,' something strange happens — sleep becomes easier. Because when you stop fighting it, the brain's alarm system quiets, and sleep can arrive on its own.
It's a paradox: giving up trying to sleep makes sleep more likely. Try it tonight, just as an experiment, okay?

third_wave_integration.description: Integration with mindfulness and ACT — the leading edge of dCBT-I in 2024–2025.

mindfulness_body_scan.description: Build non-reactive awareness of bodily sensations; reduces over-focus on internal experience pre-sleep.
mindfulness_body_scan.AI_usage: Guide users from toes to crown of the head, without judging or changing — just observing.

open_awareness.description: Open awareness of thoughts and feelings without locking onto any one (for more advanced users).
open_awareness.AI_usage: Guide users to become 'observers of the inner world' — thoughts like clouds passing, no need to follow.

ACT_commitment.description: Clarify values to shift from 'I must sleep' to 'I'm resting in a way that matters.'
ACT_commitment.AI_usage: Ask: 'If sleep weren't something to be anxious about, what would you actually want from tonight?' (Often: rest, and time with one's own quiet.)

loving_kindness.description: Build goodwill to interrupt pre-sleep social rumination.
loving_kindness.AI_usage: Guide users to send kindness toward the person they're stuck on tonight — interrupts the rumination loop.

session_structure_ai_companion.description: How the AI companion structures a dCBT-I session in a pre-sleep context.

sequence.content: Tonight's sleep difficulty (0-10), main worry (one sentence)
If worry present: validate + log + transition
Pick a suitable breathing or mindfulness practice
Difficulty + worry type + recent sleep pattern
Breathing + PMR or mindful body scan

mode_3_intensive.name: Intensive (severe insomnia, severe anxiety, possible safety risk)

sequence.content: Detailed externalization, no probing for details

insomnia_subtypes_adaptation.description: Adjust technique priorities by insomnia subtype.

sleep_onset_type.name: Sleep-Onset Insomnia
sleep_onset_type.avoid: PMR while in bed (can reinforce bed-wakefulness association)

maintenance_type.name: Sleep-Maintenance Insomnia (waking during the night)
secondary_techniques: PMR (for returning to sleep after waking)
maintenance_type.AI_guidance: When the user wakes mid-night: 'Don't look at the clock. Don't calculate hours left. Just notice — it's still night. You're still resting. Gently bring attention back to the breath.'

social_rumination_type.name: Social Rumination (pre-sleep relational worry)
social_rumination_type.AI_guidance: 'I notice tonight's worry is about someone specific. Pre-sleep replay of relationships is very common. Tonight, you don't need to solve anything. You just need to be here, well-cared-for.'

sleep_diary_tracking: Actual total sleep time (subjective is fine)
Number and total duration of nighttime awakenings

dynamic_adjustment.SE_below_80: Reduce TIB by 15-30 minutes (but never below 5 hours)
